items.b: HK$20 MILLION OF BURMESE RUBY LEADS SOTHEBY'S HONG KONG ON 17 SEPTEMBER
items.t: Earrings set with two pear-shaped Burmese rubies of 5.08 and 5.20 carats carry the top estimate in a sale of more than 200 lots. 9 of the 10 costliest lots Rapaport names are led by a coloured stone, the tenth by conch pearls; no diamond-led lot appears among them. The house publishes one figure for the earrings rather than a range, and no aggregate estimate for the sale.

items.b: BELGIUM'S PRIME MINISTER VISITS THE BHARAT DIAMOND BOURSE AS ANTWERP LEANS ON INDIA
items.t: GJEPC puts gem and jewellery trade between India and Belgium at $3.5 billion in 2025-26 and the target at $10 billion within three years. RTBF reports Antwerp traded $19.1 billion of diamonds in 2025, $19 billion of it natural, and quotes AWDC spokesperson Ine Tassignon on a 30% loss of volume and value to the Russian embargo. Between 90% and 95% of world rough is cut in India. Nothing was signed.

items.b: GARETH PENNY TELLS CIBJO'S CENTENARY CONGRESS THE DIAMOND TRADE IS IN A REAL CRISIS
items.t: The man leading the consortium bidding for De Beers opened the Vicenza congress on 4 September with an eight-point plan, five points of which concern what the trade says about its product rather than what it digs or cuts. The eighth asks De Beers to lead beyond its own business. No spend, date or funder is attached. Bloomberg put the consortium's price at about $1 billion in July.

items.b: EDGE COUNTS AUGUST JEWELRY SALES UP 5% ON 8% FEWER UNITS
items.t: The average retail sale at US independent jewellers rose 14% against August 2025. Diamond jewellery took 8% more money on 9% fewer units; coloured stones and pearls 4% more on 14% fewer. Sterling silver and alternative metals is the only line where price failed to cover volume, dollars down 5% on units down 19%. Edge publishes no store count or dollar total with the percentages.

items.b: $55,000 SAPPHIRE NECKLACE LEADS BONHAMS CALIFORNIA ON 24 SEPTEMBER
items.t: Four sapphires of 3.25, 3.32, 4.56 and 5.65 carats sit in the top lot of a sale of more than 200 pieces. The published top five all sit between $25,000 and $55,000, the band an independent shop can restock from. A three-piece gem suite holds 97.45 carats of emerald, ruby and sapphire at $35,000 to $55,000; a David Webb bangle with 1.10 carats of diamonds carries $25,000 to $35,000.

items.b: FOUR METALS HELD FRIDAY'S CLOSE FOR A THIRD SESSION AND NO METAL PRICE IS PRINTED
items.t: Kitco's board carries an identical 2026-09-04 17:00 timestamp on gold $4,429.10, silver $66.091, platinum $1,816.00 and palladium $1,368.00, matching the 05:00 tape to the cent. Under the One-Price Rule there was nothing to write back. The frozen state is established by the board's own timestamp, not by the day of the week.

tape_ts: 6 Sep 2026 - Kitco, re-read by the Editor at press time. The board answered 200 and carried an originalTime of 2026-09-04 17:00 on all four metals, a third consecutive session frozen on Friday's close and identical to the 05:00 mark to the cent, so there was nothing to write back and the 05:00 tape stands as filed. The marks are Kitco bids, this tape's convention for every metal: gold $4,429.10 (down $43.10, 0.9637%), silver $66.091 (down $0.756, 1.1309%), platinum $1,816.00 (down $1.00, 0.055%) and palladium $1,368.00 (down $33.00, 2.3555%), each against the prior session. The frozen state is read off the board's own timestamp, not off the day of the week; the page's standing 'active and trading' banner is boilerplate and is contradicted by its own originalTime. No metal price is printed anywhere in this edition. NAT1 and LGD1 on the chips below are rendered from prices.json and lab-prices.json by the build and are not this tape's marks.
